raw_text:
name: dotnet-csharp-source-generators

Creates/consumes Roslyn generators: `IIncrementalGenerator`, syntax providers, semantic analysis, emission, diagnostics, `CSharpGeneratorDriver`, NuGet packaging, `[GeneratedRegex]`, `[LoggerMessage]`, and System.Text.Json (`[JsonSerializable]`). See [skill:dotnet-roslyn-analyzers], [skill:dotnet-csharp-modern-patterns], [skill:dotnet-csharp-coding-standards]. Generators ship as analyzers targeting `netstandard2.0`.

<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
<TargetFramework>netstandard2.0</TargetFramework>
<EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>true</EnforceExtendedAnalyzerRules>
<IsRoslynComponent>true</IsRoslynComponent>
<LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Analyzers" Version="3.3.4" PrivateAssets="all" />
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp" Version="4.12.0" PrivateAssets="all" />

> **Always target `netstandard2.0`.** Generators load into the compiler process, which requires this TFM for compatibility. Use `LangVersion>latest` to write modern C# in the generator itself.

Always use `IIncrementalGenerator` over the legacy `ISourceGenerator`. Incremental generators are cache-aware and only re-run when inputs change, making them significantly faster in IDE scenarios.

public sealed class AutoNotifyGenerator : IIncrementalGenerator
public void Initialize(IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext context)

Use `ForAttributeWithMetadataName` or `CreateSyntaxProvider` with a tight predicate. Transform to simple data. Never pass `ISymbol` or `SyntaxNode` through the pipeline (they hold the compilation alive and break caching). Use `record struct` or implement `IEquatable<T>`. Same inputs must produce identical source; use `// <auto-generated/>` and `#nullable enable`. Report errors and warnings through `SourceProductionContext` rather than throwing exceptions. `Location` is not value-equatable; exclude it from equality or report before projecting to value types. Use raw string literals. File naming convention: `{TypeName}.{Feature}.g.cs`. Use `RegisterPostInitializationOutput` for independent helpers.

**Scope note:** This example targets top-level, non-generic classes for clarity. A production generator should also handle generic type parameters (emitting matching `partial class Foo<T>` declarations) and nested types (emitting nested partial class hierarchies). Report a diagnostic for unsupported shapes rather than emitting invalid code.

Use `CSharpGeneratorDriver` to run generators in-memory and verify output. Use [Verify.SourceGenerators](https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.SourceGenerators) for snapshots.

`[GeneratedRegex]`: method must be `static partial` returning `Regex`; place on `partial class` or `partial struct`. Supports all `RegexOptions` except `RegexOptions.Compiled` (which is ignored -- the source generator replaces it).

`[LoggerMessage]`: methods must be `static partial` in a `partial class`. Parameters matching `{Placeholder}` are structured data. `Exception` is logged automatically (do not include in message template). Specify explicit event IDs for stable telemetry.

JSON generation is AOT-compatible. Register all types in `[JsonSerializable]` attributes. Use `TypeInfoResolverChain` (net8.0+) to combine contexts. Required for Native AOT -- reflection-based serialization is trimmed.

<ProjectReference Include="..\MyGenerator\MyGenerator.csproj"

NuGet generators go under `analyzers/dotnet/cs/`; use `<IncludeBuildOutput>false</IncludeBuildOutput>`, `<DevelopmentDependency>true</DevelopmentDependency>`, and `<None Include="$(OutputPath)\$(AssemblyName).dll" PackagePath="analyzers/dotnet/cs" />`. Add `Generated/` to `.gitignore`.
